title: A Diagnostic Study of Multi-Agent LLMs for Real-World Debates
one_liner: Evaluate debates by measuring the quality of the interaction process, not only whether the agents converge on an answer.
lead: In real debates, especially on policy or planning questions, there may be no single ground-truth answer that makes evaluation easy. This paper shows that outcome-only scoring misses important failures. A debate can end in agreement and still be poor if one agent dominates, others stop engaging, or the group converges too early. The paper therefore measures the debate process itself because the path to the answer often reveals whether the discussion was actually useful.

problem.h2: Why outcome-only debate scores are incomplete
paras: Many current evaluations check whether agents reached consensus, whether a majority vote selected one answer, or whether another model liked the final output. Those checks can miss process failures because they focus on the endpoint. A weak debate can still produce a plausible answer by chance, while a strong debate may expose disagreement productively before arriving at a careful conclusion.

The paper builds diagnostic measures for engagement, responsiveness, influence balance, stability, and agent utility. These measures matter because they expose how the discussion unfolded, which is often where failures such as domination, sycophancy, or premature agreement first appear.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Judge debate quality by inspecting interaction patterns as well as the final answer.

panels.title: 1. Agents start a debate
panels.viz_args: Several agents discuss a policy or planning question
panels.caption: The discussion may look active even when the process is weak.

panels.title: 2. Outcome-only scoring watches the end
panels.viz_args: Did they agree? Did the final answer look good?
panels.caption: This view ignores what happened during the exchange.

panels.title: 3. Process diagnostics watch the interaction
panels.caption: The paper adds interpretable measures that describe debate health.

panels.title: 4. Hidden failures become visible
panels.viz_args: Detect domination, sycophancy, and early lock-in
panels.caption: A bad process can now be flagged even if the final answer sounds acceptable.

panels.title: 5. Evaluation matches human judgment better
panels.caption: Humans care about whether agents listened, responded, and changed views for reasons. The diagnostic view captures that.

steps.text: Collect full transcripts from real-world discussion settings where simple answer checking is weak.
Compute interpretable indicators such as how much each agent contributes and how often agents respond to each other.
Keep the usual end-result checks so that process and outcome can be compared.
Test which metrics line up better with what people judge as a healthy and useful debate so that the evaluation reflects the discussion quality humans actually care about.
Use the process metrics to identify cases of domination, disengagement, or premature convergence.

paras: The paper changes what counts as evidence of a good debate. The target is no longer only the final answer; it is the quality of the interaction that produced it.

hidden.name: Debate health
paras: Debate health is the overall quality of the interaction process: whether agents engage with the topic, respond to each other, share influence reasonably, and remain open to revision without collapsing too early. This quantity is hard to observe from only the final answer.
The paper approximates debate health with several transparent metrics. That decomposition is useful because one number alone would hide which part of the interaction failed.

heat.caption: Darker means the observed process looks healthier and more informative.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is whether this was a good discussion, not merely whether it ended with one answer.
The paper measures debate health through engagement, responsiveness, influence balance, stability, and utility because those factors reveal process failures that end-result scores miss.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: weak discussions leave structural traces
paras: Domination, sycophancy, and premature convergence are not random accidents. They change the shape of the transcript. A dominating agent speaks more and moves others without reciprocal influence. A sycophantic agent agrees without adding independent content. Premature convergence appears as quick agreement before key objections are examined. Process metrics work because these failures alter who speaks, who responds, and how opinions change.

That is why the diagnostics align better with human judgment. People notice whether a debate was balanced and responsive because those properties are part of what makes discussion trustworthy in settings where a final answer cannot be verified directly.

stages.s: Combine process view with end-result view

math.words: A compact summary is to reward engagement, responsiveness, and balance while penalizing one-sided influence. The exact paper uses several metrics, but this formula shows the intended direction.
math.equation: process_score = engagement + responsiveness + balance + stability - influence_asymmetry
symbols: overall debate quality from the process view
how actively agents contribute to the discussion
how often agents address what others actually said
how evenly influence and participation are distributed
whether opinion changes are reasoned rather than erratic
how much one agent drives the rest without comparable pushback

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Debate A: engagement 4, responsiveness 4, balance 3, stability 3, asymmetry 1, process score 13.
Debate B: engagement 3, responsiveness 1, balance 1, stability 2, asymmetry 4, process score 3.
Debate A is better because agents respond to each other and influence is not concentrated in one speaker.

math.note: The paper keeps the individual diagnostics visible because different failure types should stay distinguishable.

charts.title: Outcome-only evaluation
charts.note: End-result checks miss many process failures because they examine the answer after the discussion has already collapsed.

charts.title: Process-aware diagnostics
charts.note: Process measures work better because they inspect the interaction itself. The values are illustrative summaries of the trend reported in the paper.

items.html: Agents might learn to mention each other's points more often without adding real substance, which could raise responsiveness scores without improving the debate.

items.b: Not every domain values the same process shape.
items.html: A legal debate, a planning meeting, and a brainstorming session may need different balances of disagreement and convergence, so one universal threshold may be too rigid.
If human raters disagree about what a healthy debate looks like, the alignment target becomes fuzzy because the benchmark itself is unstable.
The main gain is diagnostic visibility because a developer can now see why a debate failed, not only that it failed.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Run a set of three-agent debates on questions that do not have one easy ground-truth answer. Save full transcripts and ask human reviewers to rate discussion quality. Then compare two evaluators: one that scores only the final answer, and one that also computes process metrics such as response rate, balance, and influence asymmetry.
The demo should show that process-aware scoring predicts human ratings better because it catches debates that sound polished at the end but were structurally weak throughout.
demo.closing: The demo must prove that transcript structure carries real evaluation signal because the route to an answer matters in open-ended debates.
